speaker: interviewer
text: Hi Elena! Thanks for doing this. Are you somewhere you can talk?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yes, I'm in the library, in one of the little booths. It's fine.

speaker: interviewer
text: Perfect. So, no wrong answers, this is just about how you shop for food.

speaker: interviewee
text: Okay, sounds good.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me a bit about your household and who does the food shopping.

speaker: interviewee
text: I'm doing a master's in chemistry and I share a flat with three other people. We each buy our own food, mostly, and then there's a shared shelf for oil and salt and stuff that nobody ever refills.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha, classic. And how did you hear about Shmuber Eats?

speaker: interviewee
text: It was on the student discount site. A big first-order discount, so I thought, okay, let's actually try it properly. We're on the fourth floor, no lift, and I'm tired of hauling water bottles up the stairs.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Walk me through your last order, from opening the app to putting things away.

speaker: interviewee
text: So I'd planned the week. I do a big curry on Sunday and eat it till Wednesday. I put in rice, onions, the spices, chickpeas, spinach, coconut milk. And putting things away I noticed instead of the coconut milk in a tin they'd given me a carton of the coconut drink, the thin one you put in cereal, which for a curry is just water, it splits.

speaker: interviewer
text: Wait, the drink instead of the tin? What did you do with the curry?

speaker: interviewee
text: I used it anyway because I had nothing else. It was sad. Very thin. I think the picker just searched coconut and took the first thing.

speaker: interviewer
text: And did you tell anyone, or contact us about it?

speaker: interviewee
text: No. I mean, who would I tell? There was no button for wrong for the recipe, only missing or damaged.

speaker: interviewer
text: Got it, that's really useful. Great. Let's move on. How often do you order groceries online?

speaker: interviewee
text: Every two weeks, more or less, since the discount. Before that, never.

speaker: interviewer
text: And on what day, usually?

speaker: interviewee
text: Saturday morning. I order Friday night when I'm too tired to go out.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. Tell me about the last time an item in your order was substituted.

speaker: interviewee
text: Apart from the coconut thing? The spinach once, they gave me frozen instead of fresh. That one was okay, it was going in a curry anyway.

speaker: interviewer
text: Did the app tell you before the delivery?

speaker: interviewee
text: It sent a message, yes, but it was after I'd already gone to bed, so I only saw it in the morning when the bags were on the doorstep.

speaker: interviewer
text: Okay. How do you keep track of what you need between orders?

speaker: interviewee
text: I have a note on my phone. The flatmates have their own. We tried a shared one for the shelf, it lasted about four days.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Great. How did you pick the delivery window last time?

speaker: interviewee
text: I picked nine to eleven on Saturday. I'm always home Saturday morning, I'm basically asleep.

speaker: interviewer
text: And is the two hours okay for you, or too long?

speaker: interviewee
text: For Saturday it's fine. On a weekday I'd be in the lab, so I just don't do weekdays.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. What would you think of a monthly delivery pass, and what would you pay for it?

speaker: interviewee
text: As a student, honestly, five maybe. Not more. I already pay for two streaming things I should cancel.

speaker: interviewer
text: Okay. Great. On a scale of one to ten, how much do you like Shmuber Eats?

speaker: interviewee
text: Eight. It's very convenient. It just needs smarter pickers, or smarter, I don't know, rules.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Would you recommend it to a friend?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yes, I already did, to my flatmate. She used my code.

speaker: interviewer
text: Amazing. What did you like most?

speaker: interviewee
text: Not carrying the water up. That's the whole thing for me.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. And what did you like least?

speaker: interviewee
text: The search on the app is weird. I search for chickpeas and it shows me hummus first.

speaker: interviewer
text: Noted, search. Great. Do you use any other grocery apps?

speaker: interviewee
text: I had one for meal kits once, but it was too expensive for me.

speaker: interviewer
text: Got it. Last question, is there anything about your orders I didn't ask about?

speaker: interviewee
text: I don't think so. Maybe just that the bags are a lot. I have a mountain of paper bags now.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha, noted. Thank you so much Elena, this was super helpful.

speaker: interviewee
text: You're welcome, bye!
